note.question: How do competing firms' security incentives differ when they earn revenue from prices versus advertising, and how should security liability or fines reflect those business models?
note.overview: Two competing firms strategically choose security and, under the paid business model, prices; consumers sort between firms while attackers choose whether to attack based on security and market share. The paper solves symmetric subgame-perfect equilibria under pricing and advertising business models and compares regulation.
